telegram.about: Messages come from your own Telegram bot. Create one with @BotFather (send /newbot), copy its token, then find your chat id (send the bot a message and open https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getUpdates, or ask @userinfobot).

help.bot_token: Given by @BotFather, like 123456789:AAH… Write-only: it is never shown again.
help.chat_id: A user id (123456789), a group id (-1001234567890) or a public channel (@name). Add the bot to the group or channel first.
help.topic_id: Only for a group with topics: the number of the topic that receives the messages.

gotify.about: Gotify is a push server you host yourself. Create an application in its web page and copy the application token.

help.server: The address of your server, for example https://gotify.example.org. On your home network tick “Allow a private-network destination” below.
help.token: The token of the application (not a client token). Write-only: it is never shown again.

home_assistant.about: Posts to a Home Assistant notify service, for example your phone's Companion app. Create a long-lived access token in your Home Assistant profile.

help.url: For example http://homeassistant.local:8123. Home Assistant is usually on your home network: tick “Allow a private-network destination” below. Only the address: a path such as /ha (Home Assistant behind a reverse proxy on a sub-path) is refused.
help.token: Profile, Security, Long-lived access tokens. Write-only: it is never shown again.
help.service: The service name without “notify.”: mobile_app_your_phone (see Developer tools, Actions). A full name such as notify.alerts works too.

pushover.about: Pushover delivers notifications to its Android and iOS app. Create an application on pushover.net (Create an Application/API Token) and copy its API token, and your user key from the dashboard. A free application may send 10,000 messages a month: Meshloom's default limits (10 a minute, 100 an hour) keep a busy mesh well below it, but the monthly quota is yours to watch.

help.user_key: Shown on your Pushover dashboard (30 characters). Write-only: it is never shown again.
help.app_token: The API token of the application you created (30 characters). Write-only: it is never shown again.
help.devices: Device names separated by commas (up to 10). Empty: every device of your account.

matrix.about: Posts to a Matrix room. Use a dedicated account (or a bot) that has joined the room; the messages are sent as Markdown.

help.server: The address of your homeserver, for example https://matrix.example.org. Only the address, no path. A server on your home network needs “Allow a private-network destination” ticked below.
help.username: Leave empty when you use an access token. With a user name, the next field is that account's password.
help.credential: An access token (leave the user name empty) or the account's password. Write-only: it is never shown again.
help.room: The room id (!abcdef:example.org, in the room settings, Advanced) or its alias (#room:example.org). The account must already be in the room.

signal.about: Sends Signal messages through a signal-cli REST API server (bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api) that you run, usually on your home network, with a registered number.

help.server: The address of the REST server, for example http://signal-api.lan:8080. On your home network tick “Allow a private-network destination” below. Only the address, no path.
help.from_number: The number registered in signal-cli, with its country code: +33600000000.
help.to: One or more numbers with their country code, separated by commas (up to 10): +33611111111,+33622222222.
help.password: Only if a reverse proxy in front of the REST server asks for a user name and password. Write-only: it is never shown again.

slack.about: Posts to the Slack channel an incoming webhook is attached to. Create the webhook in your Slack app (Incoming Webhooks), then paste its address https://hooks.slack.com/services/AAA/BBB/CCC in one piece.

help.webhook: The whole address Slack gives you, starting with https://hooks.slack.com/services/. It holds the secret: write-only, never shown again.

mattermost.about: Posts to the Mattermost channel an incoming webhook is attached to (Integrations, Incoming Webhooks). The messages are sent as Markdown.

help.server: The address of your server, for example https://mattermost.example.org (a path prefix is kept). On your home network tick “Allow a private-network destination” below.
help.token: The last part of the webhook address (…/hooks/<key>). Write-only: it is never shown again.

rocketchat.about: Posts to a Rocket.Chat room as a dedicated account that has joined it.

help.server: The address of your server, for example https://chat.example.org. Only the address, no path. On your home network tick “Allow a private-network destination” below.
help.password: The account's password, or a personal access token (then set the credential type to token). Write-only: it is never shown again.
help.room: A channel (#general), a user (@name) or a room id.
help.username: With a password, the account's user name. With a personal access token, the user ID Rocket.Chat shows next to the token (not the user name).

sms_free.about: Free Mobile sends an SMS to the line of the account that enabled the option, and to nobody else. Enable “Notifications par SMS” in your Free Mobile account to get the key. An SMS holds about 160 characters, so the text policy is fixed on “never”: only a short title is sent.

help.api_key: The key shown when you enable the option. Write-only: it is never shown again.

sms_sfr.about: Sends SMS through the SFR messaging service (an SFR account with the SMS API enabled). An SMS holds about 160 characters, so the text policy is fixed on “never”: only a short title is sent.

help.username: The login of your SFR messaging account.
help.space_id: The space (service) identifier given by SFR for your account.
help.to: One or more numbers with their country code, separated by commas (up to 10): +33600000000.
